scope: Measures the relation-reframing hypothesis in docs/COMPACT_BACKEND_LATTICE_GATE.md section 2: does proving only a hash-preimage statement (SHA256(seed)=commitment) instead of the full clamp(SHA512(seed))[0:32]=scalar AND [scalar]B=point relation reduce Binius64 Iron Spartan proof size/cost. Same pinned commit, same ZKProver/ZKVerifier configuration, same public RFC8032 test1 fixture seed as witness, and the same dummy action digest as tools/binius-seed-research, for a direct comparison. Public fixture only; not a production relation, not a security approval.

wrong_witness_measurement.scope: Actual unsatisfied-witness prover abort; NOT verifier rejection of an adversarially generated proof. Identical failure phase/exit code to tools/binius-seed-research's own wrong-witness measurement.

padding_bucket_sweep.scope: Synthetic circuits of N sequential two-input AND gates, built with the same CircuitBuilder, to characterize the committed_total_len power-of-two padding rule this backend applies independent of the actual relation. Confirms there is no fixed 2048-word floor: a trivial 1-constraint circuit pads to 4 words. The crossover from a 1024-word bucket to a 2048-word bucket falls between roughly 256 and 512 raw AND gates in this synthetic shape, which explains why both the 912-AND-constraint SHA-256 relation and the 1155-AND-constraint SHA-512+clamp+scalar-mult relation land in the same 2048-word bucket and therefore produce almost identical proof sizes.

conclusion: The relation-reframing hypothesis (prove only a hash preimage instead of the full SHA-512/clamp/scalar-mult relation) is PARTIALLY FALSIFIED for proof size and CONFIRMED for CPU time, in this exact backend/parameter configuration. Proof size: 539,856 vs 539,888 bytes -- a 32-byte difference, not the 1-2 orders of magnitude the research doc's section 2 projected, because both relations' AND-constraint counts (912 and 1155) land in the identical 2048-word padded trace bucket; removing the scalar-multiplication gadget was not enough to cross down into the 1024-word bucket. Prove time: -31% (0.748s vs 1.086s). Verify time: -42% (0.351s vs 0.601s). This sharpens, rather than removes, the case for a true algebraic ZK-friendly commitment (Vision/Poseidon-over-binary-fields) over a merely smaller classical hash like SHA-256: the padding_bucket_sweep shows real headroom exists (a circuit under roughly 256-512 raw AND gates would drop to the 1024-word or smaller bucket and measurably shrink the proof), but SHA-256's own ~900 AND constraints is not small enough to reach it. This does not close F-01: no lattice-based or algebraic-hash backend has been measured here, and this specific finding is about Binius64's Iron Spartan/BaseFold padding behavior only.
